record.paper_title: Challenges in Truncating the Hierarchy of Time-Dependent Reduced Density Matrices Equations: Open Problems
record.context_brief: Extension beyond the Hubbard-model test case
record.original_question: Do the instability, density-divergence, and fermionic-constraint-violation phenomena observed for BBGKY truncations in a finite Hubbard model persist in small molecules and more complex correlated-electron systems, and how can the proposed partial remedies be validated in those settings?

evidence.quote: although here we illustrate only the performance of all the approximations for the Hubbard model, our preliminary results for small molecules also exhibit very similar issues (work in progress [36]).

We propose some partial solutions of such problem and point the main paths for future work in order to make this approach applicable for the description of the correlated electron dynamics in complex systems.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an interacting fermionic many-body system whose state is described by reduced density matrices (RDMs) $ho^{(p)}$ of orders $p=1,2,\dots$, satisfying the time-dependent BBGKY hierarchy: each $ho^{(p)}$ evolves according to an equation that couples it to $ho^{(p+1)}$. A standard practical scheme truncates this hierarchy at second order by keeping the coupled evolution equations for the one-body matrix $ho^{(1)}$ and the two-body matrix $ho^{(2)}$, while approximating the three-body matrix $ho^{(3)}$ by a closure expressed in terms of $ho^{(1)}$ and $ho^{(2)}$ (e.g. cluster expansions that neglect or partially keep the genuine three-body correlation). 

For finite Hubbard lattices driven out of equilibrium, such truncations are known to display three pathological phenomena: (i) dynamical instability of the time evolution; (ii) divergence of local densities $n_i(t)=\langle c_i^\dagger c_iangle(t)$; and (iii) violation of $N$-representability conditions for fermions, in particular loss of positive semidefiniteness of $ho^{(2)}$ and of the hole-hole and particle-hole matrices, together with violation of the antisymmetry/contraction sum rules connecting $ho^{(2)}$ and $ho^{(1)}$. Several partial remedies have been proposed, including purification/projection schemes that restore positivity at each time step and minimally-invasive corrections of the equations of motion that enforce contraction consistency.

Problem. Determine whether the three pathologies (i)–(iii) above persist in the time-dependent BBGKY truncations at the two-body level when the underlying system is (a) a small molecule described by an ab initio electronic Hamiltonian in a finite single-particle basis, and (b) more general correlated-electron systems beyond Hubbard-type lattice models. Furthermore, formulate and validate, in these settings, the proposed partial remedies (positivity-restoring purification of $ho^{(2)}$ and contraction-preserving corrections), establishing whether they yield stable, density-bounded, and $N$-representable time evolutions of $ho^{(1)}$ and $ho^{(2)}$ under external driving.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work has partially addressed the problem. Projective purification schemes for the time-dependent two-body reduced density matrix (TD2RDM) and minimal-invasive correction algorithms have been developed and shown to stabilize the BBGKY truncation at second order in quench dynamics of the Fermi-Hubbard model. However, systematic validation of these remedies for small molecules and general correlated-electron systems beyond Hubbard models has not been comprehensively established in the literature surveyed, so the broader question remains only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Projective purification of correlated reduced density matrices
status_evidence.snippet: projective purification schemes for the TD2RDM method show superior stability achieved in quench dynamics of the Fermi-Hubbard model
status_evidence.claim: A purification scheme stabilizes the truncated BBGKY hierarchy in Hubbard quench dynamics, providing a partial remedy.

status_evidence.title: Applications of Time-Dependent Density-Matrix Approach
status_evidence.snippet: role of compatibility between hierarchical equations and positive semidefiniteness of reduced density matrices in the instability of electron dynamics
status_evidence.claim: Instability and N-representability violation of truncated BBGKY are still active research topics.

status_evidence.snippet: minimal-invasive correction algorithm of the equation of motion can stabilize the BBGKY hierarchy truncated at the second order
